transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04 15:30 PDT
Duration: 38 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Daniel Cho (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (CTO, Evergreen AI), Liam O'Connor (Lead ML Eng), Zoe Kim (PM)
Shared links: quickstart deck https://redwood.ai/deck/quickstart , security pack https://redwood.ai/security/pk , benchmark sheet (shared during call)

[00:00] Sofia Martinez: hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Sofia, I'm the AE on this account, with me is Daniel our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
[00:06] Maya Patel: hey Sofia yeah doing well thanks, excited to learn more, we've been poking at a few providers.
[00:10] Liam O'Connor: yeah hello, Liam here. our main thing is minimizing time-to-first-token for our prod feature and keeping costs reasonable.
[00:18] Sofia Martinez: perfect, that's exactly what this quickstart is built for; we usually cover a short overview, how the free credits and quickstart work, and then Daniel can do a little tech Q&A—sound good?
[00:25] Zoe Kim: sounds great.
[00:27] Daniel Cho: quick intro from me, I focus on latency/cost tuning, batching and private deployments — happy to jump into any details.
[00:33] Sofia Martinez: quick housekeeping: we have a PLG self-serve flow, you can sign up, get free credits and call the hosted API in minutes. time-to-first-token often under 5 minutes for simple tests, end-to-end token including onboarding emails and keys can be 10-15 mins.
[00:48] Maya Patel: okay that's promising. can you explain what the free credits cover? is it for hosted only or also for Dedicated evaluation?
[00:55] Sofia Martinez: free credits are for hosted API usage primarily — they let you run evals and prototypes. for Dedicated we typically do a trial/POC with reserved capacity; Dedicated trials are done case-by-case and often involve a short commitment.
[01:07] Liam O'Connor: got it. our privacy team will want to understand data retention—if we use hosted, do you ingest or retain prompts?
[01:14] Daniel Cho: good question, short answer: hosted has options. by default production logging is kept for X days but we offer no-retention modes and encryption at rest via KMS. for PHI/PII-sensitive use cases we recommend Redwood Private — VPC or on-prem — where logs never leave your network.
[01:31] Maya Patel: and Private would be a separate contract / install? what's the typical timeline?
[01:36] Daniel Cho: Private requires an enterprise engagement; typical on-prem or VPC deployment is 4-8 weeks depending on scope — integrations like SSO and KMS add time. Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) can be started faster, weeks rather than months.
[01:48] Zoe Kim: do you have SOC2 reports and ISO stuff? our auditor asked for SOC2 and SAML support.
[01:54] Sofia Martinez: yes we're SOC 2 Type II and support SAML/SSO, RBAC, audit logs. I'll send the security pack with the SOC2 report and a checklist.
[02:03] Liam O'Connor: for the quickstart, we mainly want to test throughput at around 50 QPS and p95 latency under 250ms if possible. is that realistic on hosted?
[02:12] Daniel Cho: depends on model + prompt length. For small chat-type prompts and a quantized 13B on GPU, 50 QPS can be handled on hosted with batching and prefetched KV cache; p95 250ms is tight at 50QPS unless you use our low-latency routing and smaller model variants. We often recommend a two-tier approach: hosted for development and early PLG, then Dedicated for predictable p95 at scale.
[02:33] Maya Patel: can you explain that two-tier approach? what's the operational difference?
[02:37] Daniel Cho: hosted = managed by Redwood, you hit our API endpoints, we autoscale and route requests. Dedicated = you reserve capacity, you get predictable throughput and data isolation. Private = full customer-managed deployment. For Dedicated we give SLAs, capacity guarantees and can pin model versions.
[02:53] Sofia Martinez: and cost wise Dedicated is a commit model, usually better unit economics if you're consistently at scale. Hosted is pay-as-you-go — easier to start.
[03:01] Zoe Kim: we have an internal timeline — want to go from prototype to a pilot in 6-8 weeks. is that workable?
[03:07] Daniel Cho: yes prototype on hosted in days, pilot on Dedicated in 4-6 weeks if you move fast on procurement and we size capacity. Private would be longer.
[03:15] Liam O'Connor: any special infra work for us to test the API? we use k8s and have a VPC, would it require firewall changes?
[03:21] Daniel Cho: for hosted, you'll need outbound HTTPS egress to our API endpoints and to accept webhooks if you want callbacks. For Private/VPC there are VPC peering or private link options; Daniel: note — sometimes customers say "K8s ingress" but what we need is simple egress rules, no inbound unless using private link.
[03:37] Maya Patel: how about model variants / quantization — can you run int8 or 4-bit to reduce cost?
[03:42] Daniel Cho: yes we support quantized variants; Redwood Optimize can recommend which quantization profile fits your workload. Quantization reduces memory and cost but may affect output quality; we recommend A/B testing on eval prompt sets.
[03:54] Sofia Martinez: are there any gotchas with the quickstart? we sometimes see folks forget to rotate API keys or mix prod/test keys.
[04:00] Zoe Kim: good to know. do you have SDKs?
[04:03] Sofia Martinez: yes JS/Python SDKs and curl examples in the quickstart deck.
[04:08] Liam O'Connor: what's the expected p50/p95 on the hosted small model? like 7B quantized?
[04:13] Daniel Cho: rough numbers: 7B quantized on a good GPU can be p50 ~40-60ms for single-token micro-benchmarks but real chat with generation will be higher; p95 depends on sequence length. We'll share our benchmark sheet with sample numbers; you should run with your prompts for accurate numbers.
[04:29] Maya Patel: ok please share the benchmark sheet. also on compliance, we need to know about key management — can we use our KMS/HSM?
[04:36] Daniel Cho: yes for Private and Dedicated we integrate with customer KMS; hosted also supports customer-managed keys for encryption at rest via KMS integration.
[04:44] Zoe Kim: any limits on streaming / function calling? we plan to use tool calls and structured outputs.
[04:49] Daniel Cho: streaming is supported on hosted and Dedicated; function/tool calling works across. For heavy streaming load we sometimes recommend Dedicated if you have many concurrent long-lived streams.
[04:59] Sofia Martinez: want to talk through an example onboarding flow? sign up, get free credits, create API key, run quickstart curl example, hit endpoint, check responses. Time-to-first-token typically 5-10 mins for devs.
[05:11] Liam O'Connor: that matches what we want. can you issue a trial account for 2 engineers and credit for a week?
[05:16] Sofia Martinez: yes we can do that — I'll provision a trial for two seats and $500 in credits to run evaluations.
[05:22] Maya Patel: great. we'll also need a security review — can you share SOC2 and SAML docs?
[05:27] Sofia Martinez: yes will send security pack link after the call; includes SOC2, SAML docs, data flow diagrams.
[05:33] Zoe Kim: any notes on procurement — typical contract length for Dedicated?
[05:36] Sofia Martinez: Dedicated is usually monthly or annual commits; we can tailor for POC pilots. Procurement folks often ask for an MSA, SOW and an order form.
[05:44] Maya Patel: what's the pricing ballpark for Dedicated? just a rough to set expectations.
[05:48] Sofia Martinez: depends on capacity; we'll send ranges but typical reserved capacity for a mid-sized pilot might be in the tens of thousands per month; hosted will be usage-based so lower entry cost. I'll include concrete examples in the pricing email.
[05:58] Liam O'Connor: for our backend, we do heavy batching already; curious if Redwood supports continuous batching or should we implement client-side?
[06:05] Daniel Cho: Redwood runtime supports continuous server-side batching and KV cache optimizations. For best results you can do client-side grouping too; we'll share recommendations based on your traffic pattern.
[06:15] Maya Patel: any examples of customers in regulated industries?
[06:18] Sofia Martinez: yes a few healthcare and finance customers run under Dedicated or Private deployments; we can connect you to references if helpful.
[06:25] Zoe Kim: ok sounds good.
[06:27] Sofia Martinez: recap of next steps: I'll send pricing + quickstart + security pack and provision trial credits; Daniel will share benchmark sheet and a perf plan; Maya will share architecture and any data residency constraints. we'll tentatively schedule a technical deep dive mid-March.
[06:44] Maya Patel: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[06:46] Liam O'Connor: thanks all.
[06:47] Sofia Martinez: thanks, we'll follow up with the links and the creds.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-words in auto transcription (KV cache -> KV cash; SSO sometimes transcribed as S S O), speaker labels approximate.

End of transcript.
